title: Community Appointment Days compared with standard physiotherapy for people with muscle, bone or joint conditions
official: Community Appointment Days vs standard physiotherapy for people with a musculoskeletal condition
summary:
Background and study aims
One in three people have a musculoskeletal condition affecting their muscles, bones or joints. This can cause pain, difficulty moving, time off work, and increased chance of conditions like heart disease.

Physiotherapy is standard care which helps, but wait lists are long and there are not many other options.  

Community Appointment Days or ‘CADs’ offer an appointment to help people with their musculoskeletal condition, and other health and social care needs.  

This study wants to see if Community Appointment Days or ‘CADs’ should be a part of musculoskeletal care or not. If the study finds that CADs are helpful, it will also tell us how to make sure as many people can benefit from CAD as possible.  

Who can participate?
Patients 18 years or older, on a musculoskeletal outpatient therapy service wait list at a participating site, who have not attended a CAD before will be eligible.

What does the study involve?
This study compares two ways of providing care. Instead of assigning individual people to different groups, 16 NHS Trusts, across England, Scotland, and Wales will be assigned at random to offer CADs or continue with usual physiotherapy care. Individual consent is for research data collection.  

If a site is assigned to offer a CAD, patients will invited to a CAD at a community venue and offered:  

1. A ‘What Matters to You’ conversation
2. 1:1 therapy assessment  
3. Rehabilitation and advice  
4. Health promotion (blood pressure, glucose, cholesterol tests and BMI)  
5. Access to additional health and social care services  
6. Access to local council, voluntary sector and other support organisations.

Patients will be invited to complete questionnaires before and 3- and 6-months after their first appointment. Some patients and healthcare professionals will be invited to interview/focus groups to share their experience.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating:
There are no apparent benefits to taking part in this study, but results from this study might help improve healthcare of patients in the future. There is no payment for taking part.  The possible risks of taking part in the study are minimal. It might be difficult to answer some of the questions or could bring up feelings of sadness or distress. Participants do not have to answer any questions that they do not want to answer, and they can decide not to continue with the questionnaire and/or interview at any point.

Where is the study run from?
Queen Mary University of London (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
January 2027 to March 2030

Who is funding the study?
National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Professor Katie Sheehan k.sheehan@qmul.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Main study: 
Participants will be included if they are: 
1. At least 18 years of age 
2. On a musculoskeletal outpatient therapy service wait list at a participating site 
3. Have not previously attended a Community Appointment Day (CAD)
4. Not currently enrolled in other trials 
5. Provide consent (for sites willing to invite those who lack capacity to consent to their CAD, a personal or nominated consultee will be sought to provide a declaration on their behalf) 
6. At Scottish sites, adults with capacity to consent for themselves  

Process evaluation
Patient Participants: A subset of patient participants purposively sampled to take part in qualitative interviews (up to 1 - hour duration) as part of a process evaluation. This includes patients who: 
1. Attended a CAD
2. Accepted a CAD but did not attend
3. Declined CAD/standard care

Professional participants: 
1. Professionals involved in CAD delivery (managers, commissioners and staff) will be invited to complete a survey. A subset of managers, commissioners or staff employed at one of five CAD delivery sites selected for additional qualitative data collection will be purposefully sampled for the process evaluation
2. Research delivery staff from first eight sites randomised to CAD/standard care for interview to feedback on site set up and delivery
Exclusion criteria:
Do not meet the inclusion criteria.
